verdict.rationale: Letta's own docs describe self-hosting the core product. A self-hosted App Server runs agents on your own always-on machine, the agent harness can be deployed as a service, and in local mode all agent state stays on-device with no Letta account required. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted deployment, deployment detail such as install or container setup and hardware requirements, and parity for features like shared memory, which is documented as hosted in Letta Cloud.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Letta agents can run entirely on infrastructure you control
Self-hosted App Server: Run the Letta App Server to host local agents on a central, always-on machine and expose them to client applications through the Agent SDK
all agent state, including messages, memory, and provider connections, stays on-device, and no Letta account is required.
The Letta App Server lets you deploy the Letta agent harness as a service.
This default local mode stores agent state on your machine and does not require a Letta login.
